page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8i.3xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 12-vCPU Intel Xeon 8475B processor clocked at 2.7 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The server provides 96.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio with exactly 8.0 GB of RAM allocated per core. It operates without dedicated GPU hardware acceleration.

Storage and networking configurations reflect a networked architecture. The instance includes no local storage volumes, requiring external network block storage for persistent operating system and application data. Network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps, and the system is provisioned without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring supplementary routing or elastic IP allocations for external network egress.

From an efficiency perspective, the hardware profile offers high memory density relative to compute resources. With 8 GB of RAM per vCPU, it avoids the expense of overprovisioning core counts merely to meet high RAM capacity demands. However, architectural tradeoffs include total reliance on remote storage latency and throughput limitations, as well as the absence of hardware accelerators.

The ecs.r8i.3xlarge is suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand local high-IOPS scratch disks. Primary deployment profiles include in-memory databases, distributed caches such as Redis or Memcached, relational databases with moderate I/O profiles, enterprise application servers, and memory-heavy ETL batch processing pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8i.3xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated 12-vCPU Intel Xeon 8475B processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 96.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio suited for workloads requiring high memory density without excessive compute allocations. The configuration does not include local storage disks, necessitating network-attached block volumes for system and runtime persistence. It features a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps and includes no bundled GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Given its hardware layout, the instance is engineered for memory-bound tasks, including in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, enterprise ERP systems, and memory-intensive data transformation workflows.
